samples: This program runs a small web service on port 8080 that exposes a health check and a temperature converter: you give it a Celsius value as a query parameter, and it replies with JSON containing both the Celsius and Fahrenheit values. It returns clear error responses when the value is missing or not a number, and a not-found response for any other path. It needs console and network socket access, prints a startup message, and keeps running until you stop it, so it suits a simple demo or a starting point for a larger API rather than anything that needs more than this one conversion.

This program runs a small web service on port 8080 that answers a health check and converts a Celsius temperature, passed as a query parameter, into Fahrenheit, returning both values as JSON. It replies with an error message if the temperature is missing or not a number, and with "not found" for any other path. It prints a startup message, uses the console and a network socket, and keeps serving until you stop the process.

This program runs a small web service on port 8080 that offers a health check and a temperature converter. Given a Celsius value in the query string, the converter returns JSON with both the Celsius and Fahrenheit values. If the value is missing or isn't a number, it returns a "bad request" error, and any other path returns "not found". It needs console output and network socket access, and it runs until you stop the process, so it suits a simple demo or a base for a small API.

This program runs a small web service on port 8080 that offers a health check and a temperature converter. Sending a Celsius value in the query string of the convert path returns JSON with both the Celsius and Fahrenheit values. A missing or non-numeric value gets a "bad request" reply, and any other path gets "not found". It needs console and network socket permissions and runs until you stop it, so it suits a quick demo or a template for a Renyi server rather than a full application.

This program runs a small web service on port 8080 that offers two endpoints: a health check that replies "ok", and a temperature converter. The converter takes a Celsius value from the query string and returns JSON with both the Celsius and Fahrenheit values. It answers with an error message if the value is missing or isn't a number, and it returns a not-found response for any other path. It needs console and network socket access, and it runs until the process is stopped.
